RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the August 5, 2003/Sravana 14, 1925 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Civil Aviation; Finance, Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—155
361
Losses suffered by airports
1642. DR. ABRAR AHMED:
SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the names of airports which are
running into losses;
(b) the accumulated losses in each case
as on 31st March, 2003;
(c) the main reasons for losses; and
(d) the steps taken to minimise the
losses?
Revamping IA's functioning
1643. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MISS MABEL REBELLO:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that bad deals in
IA had cost Rs. 32.15 crores on account of
under-utilization of code share capacity and
non-payment of dues by international
airlines;
(b) whether the lower revenue is
attributed to frequent changes in flight
schedules, high rate of cancellation
of tickets by agents, poor punctuality
and operations on uneconomic routes;
and
(c) if so, action plan of Government to
control unabated loss and to revamp its
functioning?
Private sector participation in
setting up of airports
1644. MISS MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to rope in private sector for setting
up airports, if so, the details of the joint
venture project;
(b) whether Government have already
listed architect firms for the design of new
projects; and
(c) whether this poses any kind of
security risk?

Request for more seats by
Emirates
1645. SHRI PARMESHWAR
KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Emirates
Airlines has requested Government to
increase its seats in the Indian Sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is Government's reaction
thereto?
Regular flights to Kanpur
1646. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION  be
pleased to state:
(a) what steps are being taken by
Government to provide regular air flights
to Kanpur, a commercial city of Uttar
Pradesh; and
(b) if not, the reasons therefor?
Comprehensive map for
development of civil aviation
1647. SHRI ABANI ROY:
SHRI R.P. GOENKA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a
comprehensive road map for the
development of civil aviation sector is being
prepared;
(b) if so, the outline thereof  together
with its present status;
(c) the details of the areas identified for
focussed attention and thrust to make air
travel affordable and hassle-free and also
to improve the operational efficiency of
the aviation industry so as to face
competition from the private airlines; and
(d) the steps taken/being taken to
ascertain the views of the various concerned
interests in formulating the new road map?
Recovery of dues from travel
agents
1648. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that failure of
Indian Airlines to ensure proper and timely
remittance of dues has resulted in a blockage
of huge amount which runs into several
crores of rupees with the Travel Agents
authorised by the I.A.;
(b) if so, the details thereof as on
31st March, 2003;
(c) how much amount is outstanding
against them for the last two years; and
(d) what steps have been taken to
recover the outstanding dues?
New concession rules for Senior
Citizens
1649. SHRI N.R. DASARI:
SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that  new rules
have been introduced w.e.f. 7th July, 2003
for concession to Senior Citizens in Indian
Airlines;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that this new
rule will restrict the air travels by the Senior
Citizens for some pre-arranged tourist

purposes only and not for any emergencies;
and
(d) if so, whether Government will
consider withdrawal of the new rules?
Restoration of air links with
Pakistan
1650. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Pakistan has sought an
agreement with India to prevent any
unilateral banning of overflights in future
by either country;
(b) if so, whether Pakistan has suggested
a meeting of civil aviation officials of the
two countries to ensure that one party
would not be able to withdraw the
overflight rights of the other;
(c) whether Pakistan had offered to
restore only flight connections between the
two countries and not overflights; and
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto
and the final decision taken in this regard?
Losses due to pilots' strike
